findings.text: Provides architecture dirty-log enablement for a masked portion of a slot, ensuring large mappings become amenable to small-granularity tracking under manual protection mode and choosing the appropriate clearing or protection mechanism according to available CPU logging support.
Clears dirty tracking state for guest frames selected by a mask, covering both two-dimensional paging structures and reverse-map structures whenever each mechanism is present.

Offers a best-effort request to reduce large mappings toward a target page size across shadow and two-dimensional paging structures when the latter is active, with no TLB maintenance required at the call site.
Reports the per-VM size of the CPU-assisted dirty logging area.

Exposes guest-frame aging queries that consult two-dimensional paging structures and shadow reverse maps as applicable, with a mutating variant that clears accessed state and a non-mutating probe that preserves state and can exit early on a positive indication.
Shadow mappings are considered possibly present when two-dimensional paging is inactive or when a counter of indirect shadow pages is non-zero, gating whether reverse-map aging work is attempted.
Accessed state of a shadow entry is determined by a global accessed mask.

Reverse-map insertion associates a shadow entry with its guest frame and access rights, accounts the mapping in per-level statistics, records peak list growth, and recycles excessively long lists by zapping and flushing the affected frame.

Slot reverse-map walker carries input slot with frame interval and level bounds, exposes current frame with its head and level, and retains a private end marker to bound traversal to populated entries.
Small page vector holds a bounded array of page-plus-index pairs with a count, using a negative sentinel to mark absence of an index.
Traversal path records ancestors and child positions sized for the maximum supported paging depth, advanced by helpers that fill levels from a page vector.
Shadow allocation context groups caches for page headers, page storage, and shadowing metadata.
Defines a predicate callback type over VM state returning a boolean decision, with remaining parameters beyond the initial VM handle not visible in this fragment.

Child page role is derived from its parent by moving one level down, installing requested access and directness, clearing passthrough and invalid flags, and encoding address-space quartering for guests with narrow page-table entries.

Child acquisition reuses an existing present non-large mapping when its frame and full role match, signalling existence rather than allocating, otherwise obtains a shadow page for the requested frame and role.

Shadow walk progresses from root initialization through validity checks to stepwise descent, handling invalid or dummy roots, reduced-depth roots, and legacy extended roots, then yielding entry locations until an absent or terminal entry ends traversal.

Linking a shadow page replaces any conflicting mapping with appropriate invalidation, installs a non-leaf entry with access-tracking awareness, records the new parent relationship, and propagates unsynchronized marking when the child carries such state.

Unsynchronized marking is sticky per child position and counted per page, propagating once from child to ancestors, while explicit unsynchronization of a page records statistics and then triggers ancestor propagation.

Lookup of the shadow-page hash requires holding the VM memory-management lock and observes the table pointer with acquire ordering to synchronize with out-of-lock publication, substituting an empty table when none is published.
Reverse-map aging iterates under a read-only guard with lockless entry access, while two-dimensional paging aging holds read-copy-update protection across filtered roots and leaf entries.

Aging and reclamation avoid blocking and retry on races, treat concurrently modified entries as still young, skip mirrored entries during age-out, and restrict the two-dimensional aging helper to valid roots and non-unmapping use.
Direct mapping validation discards a child link and flushes translation caches when the recorded access no longer matches the required access.
Zapping through a reverse-map head delegates to bulk removal of all associated shadow entries and reports whether any work was done.
Write-flooding accounting for a shadow page can be cleared through its entry pointer.
Architecture dirty-log enablement and frame aging queries serve as entry points from memory-management and reclaim paths into MMU dirty and accessed handling.
Reverse-map recycle threshold is 1000 entries.
Page vector capacity is 16 entries.
Invalid child position sentinel is -1.
Parent tracking ignores a null parent pointer and otherwise records the parent entry in the child page parent list using the supplied allocation cache.
Two-dimensional root iteration is scoped by address-space identifier and root type, skipping non-matching roots.
Shadow entry position within a table is derived from the guest address and traversal level using the standard page-table indexing width for shadow entries.
Whether access and dirty tracking is disabled for a shadow page is carried in its role.
